paragraphs: Rav Chiyya bar Adda, son of Bar Kappara's sister, died. They told R. Yochanan, “Enter and eulogize him.” He said, “Let R. Shimon ben Lakish enter, for he knows his strength in Torah”: Kohelet Rabbah, on “Sweet is the sleep of the worker.” Chazit Rabbah, on “My beloved went down to his garden,” has Chiyya bar Avya, a scribal error. They told R. Yochanan, “Enter and eulogize him.” He said, “Let Resh Lakish enter, for he is his student and knows his strength.” Resh Lakish entered, etc. In Jerusalem Berakhot, chapter 2, mishnah 8, Resh Lakish lamented him because he was his teacher: a person's student is dear like his son, etc. Yefeh Mareh explains: Resh Lakish cried and wept; the Targum of “when he cries to Me” is “when he calls before Me.” R. Chiyya was Resh Lakish's student. In Yalkut on Song of Songs, on “My beloved went down to his garden”: when R. Chiyya bar Abba, son of Bar Kappara's sister, died, Resh Lakish entered and eulogized him. This is in Jerusalem Talmud, Mi SheMetu. R. Chiyya bar Adda: Jerusalem Horayot, chapter 3, end of halakhah 5. In R. Acha's name: Jerusalem Berakhot, chapter 6, end of mishnah 1. In R. Chanina's name: Arba Mitot. He asked before R. Yochanan: Maaserot, chapter 1. He asked before R. Mana: Shekalim, chapter 4; Maaserot, chapter 5. In Resh Lakish's name: end of Osin Passin and end of chapter 1 of Terumot. In the Babylonian Talmud, Ketubot 111b, R. Chiyya bar Abba taught Resh Lakish's young children; he was absent for three days and did not come. See R. Chiyya bar Abba above, and what I wrote there. See Bar Pada, son of Bar Kappara's sister, above. I find it difficult to emend this to R. Chiyya bar Pada, who was Bar Kappara's sister's son, or to say that there it should read “Adda, his sister's son.”
